newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic sees major interconnect deals.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic sees major interconnect deals.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp said on Thursday it expected to have local interconnection deals with AT&T Corp , MCI Communications Corp and Sprint Corp before it applies to enter long distance service.

Bell Atlantic, which is in the process of merging with NYNEX Corp, needs to meet a competitive checklist for competition in its local calling region before it can offer long distance service in that region.
"By the time we apply I am sure we will have (interconnection) agreements in place with AT&T, MCI and Sprint," said Bell Atlantic general counsel James Young.
"We are targeting early 1997 to meet the checklist requirements," said James Cullen, Bell Atlantic vice chairman. Cullen and Young were holding an informal press briefing.
Bell Atlantic is planning to apply for long distance in its own region within 90 days of meeting the checklist, and expects long distance approvals by the middle of 1997.

While Bell Atlantic has made dozens of agreements or partial agreements to connect its local network in various states with small rivals, neither it nor any regional Bell has made a deal with the three big long distance competitors.
In each of Bell Atlantic's six states and the District of Columbia, talks with each of the big three are in arbitration.

Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt has been quoted as saying that deals with the big three will be necessary to meet the checklist, but the Bells dispute this interpretation of the 1996 Telecom Act.

Cullen and Young said they did not expect the recent court suspension of the FCC pricing guidelines for resale of local circuits to slow the process of opening local markets. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1610
